messages:
maria.marketing: Hey team — quick sync: we need a short, customer-friendly status page update + comms timing for the partial degradation this morning. Also thinking about a short banner for the webinar registration page (we don't want to scare registrants). Can we draft copy and agree when marketing should post vs when support posts to customers?

alex.support: Do we have a clear impact statement yet? who/what is affected?

jordan.prod: API gateway had elevated errors for text-generation endpoints between 08:14 and 08:42 UTC. Some requests retried and succeeded; a subset saw 5xx until the rollout at 08:42. No data loss.

oncall-bot: Incident INC-2026-042: elevated 5xx on hosted text-generation endpoints detected at 08:14 UTC. Auto-rollback executed at 08:41 UTC, mitigation confirmed at 08:42 UTC.

alex.support: Thanks. So customer impact: intermittent 5xx (retries recommended), post-08:42 service restored. We should call out timeframe and mitigation.

nina.comm: Draft status copy suggestion below — short for status page and an expanded email paragraph. PTAL and flag any legal/ops issues.

nina.comm: ```Status page (short):
We experienced intermittent errors affecting text-generation API endpoints between 08:14–08:42 UTC. The issue has been mitigated; requests may have been retried or returned 5xx during that window. No customer data was compromised. We are investigating root cause and will post an update within 48 hours.

Customer email (paragraph):
Earlier today, some customers experienced intermittent errors (5xx) when calling Redwood's text-generation endpoints between 08:14 and 08:42 UTC. Our on-call team detected elevated errors and performed a rollback to a safe configuration; service was restored at 08:42 UTC. We believe no customer data was affected. If you continue to see errors, please reach out to support@redwood.ai and include request IDs and timestamps. We will follow up with a post-incident summary once the investigation completes.```

sam.sales: That reads well. Quick ask: for leads coming through webinar signups — should we send a small heads-up email from SDRs saying "we noticed an outage earlier" or just the normal nurture? Concerned about scaring prospects.

maria.marketing: Good question. My recommendation: do NOT email prospects proactively about the outage unless they were directly affected (customer accounts or high-value leads we can confirm had failures). For webinar registrants, add a subtle note on the registration page: "We experienced a brief service disruption that has been resolved — services are operating normally." link to status. That way trust is preserved without overcommitting.

alex.support: Agree. For customers with open tickets or high value, CS/AE can reach out with tailored notes. Support will send a follow-up to anyone who filed incidents.

jordan.prod: Ops is ok with the status wording. We should avoid saying "rollback" in the public status if possible — ops prefers "mitigation performed". Nina, can you swap that phrasing?

nina.comm: Will do. Updated line: "Our on-call team detected elevated errors and performed a mitigation; service was restored at 08:42 UTC."

maria.marketing: Great. Proposed timeline: marketing posts status page update now (short copy), support threads and customer emails go out in next 30–60 mins to affected customers only, and we hold the webinar banner update (small note + link to status) queued for the next deploy. Any objections?

sam.sales: No objections. Sales will prep a 1-paragraph SDR template for any warm leads flagged by support.

alex.support: Support will compile list of affected customers and open tickets — will update in #support-updates within 20m.

nina.comm: I'll publish the status page snippet in 5 mins and paste the final link here.

oncall-bot: Update logged: INC-2026-042 status update posted by nina.comm at 08:55 UTC.

maria.marketing: Thanks everyone — please add any follow-ups in thread. I'll coordinate the webinar copy after Nina drops the final status link. :thumbsup:
